claim: Human behavioural-science samples are overwhelmingly WEIRD (68% US, 96% Western industrialized in top journals 2003-2007), so most 'human' reasoning findings are claims about a narrow group.
agent_test: Tag each human-evidence line with population tested; check agent downgrades single-population claims at equal tokens.

claim: Cross-cultural reasoning differences (rule vs family resemblance) in Norenzayan 2002 Study 2 are instruction-dependent: under 'belong to' European American 69% and East Asian 70% chose rules; under 'similar to' EA 69% rule vs East Asian 41%. Many Labs 2 (N=7,396) found the instruction effect d=0.86, larger than the original, and the WEIRD advantage reversed under 'similar to' (42.8% WEIRD vs 48.4% less WEIRD rule use).
agent_test: Run same reasoning item with and without salience/instruction cues; measure whether the agent's answer flips.

claim: All groups in Norenzayan 2002 were strongly sensitive to logical validity (F=1161.73); the cultural belief-bias difference was small beside shared validity sensitivity, supporting universal core reasoning with style differences at the margin.
agent_test: Report validity sensitivity separately from bias in any agent test of belief bias.

claim: Analytic-vs-holistic differences in perception and attention are weaker than the founding studies suggested: several replications find little or no robust East-West difference in visual cognition tasks and contradiction judgments.
agent_test: Do not hard-code a 'cultural style' module; test agent only on tasks where effects replicate.

claim: Face-scanning differences (Blais 2008) are real as strategy but yield equal accuracy; a spotlight design (Caldara 2010) found no culture x aperture interaction on accuracy (F(2,54)=0.6), consistent with universal information use.
agent_test: Check equal accuracy under different strategies before inferring different competence.

claim: Many Labs 2: across 125 samples/36 countries, only 3 of 28 effects were moderated by WEIRD-vs-non-WEIRD split, but power to detect cultural moderation was low (28%) and sites were culturally close to the US, so absence of moderation is weak evidence of universality. Many Labs 2 full text: median original d=0.60 vs replication d=0.15; 32% opposite direction; WEIRD split was binary, not continuous distance.
agent_test: Weight 'universal' verdicts by power and by cultural distance of samples, not by non-significance.

claim: Small-scale societies and non-WEIRD groups show different values on perceptual and sorting tasks (Segall illusions, Mapuche/Sangu holistic sorting, rod-and-frame), placing Western undergraduates at the extreme end of distributions rather than as the norm.
agent_test: Treat Western-undergraduate results as one end of a distribution when estimating base rates.

claim: Rice-wheat differences: observational studies are confounded by climate, income and history; one quasi-random natural experiment (two Chinese state farms, Talhelm 2024) found rice farmers more holistic (B=0.28, p=.025, r=.15), more loyal to friends (r=.18) and less self-inflating (r=.18), at about half the East-West gap. Only two farms and the original lab; no independent replication found.
agent_test: Require a causal design or a second independent sample before the agent accepts a cultural-cause claim.

claim: Confounded designs are a standard critique: economic-game offers can reflect different scenario meanings, not different fairness reasoning; matched-context designs are proposed.
agent_test: When comparing two prompts/personas, hold context constant and vary one factor.

claim: Jin et al. 2023 found GPT-3.5/GPT-4 more holistic than human norms on scales (AHS 5.35 and 5.01 vs 4.87), but the design had 10 runs, temperature 1, different norm studies, and self-report scales, so it does not show LLMs reason holistically.
agent_test: Replicate with behavioural tasks, more runs, same-study human norms.

claim: LLM 'cultural tendencies' are fragile: prompt language had d=0.045 (eta2=0.0002), framing d=-2.095 (eta2=0.542), model origin d=0.169, in 8 models at temperature 0; prompt framing dwarfs culture. Prompt-format variance is large on standard benchmarks too (Sclar 2024: median 7.5 points, up to 76).
agent_test: Vary framing and language at equal tokens; report variance share per factor.

claim: Prompting in a language does not reliably switch an LLM's cognitive style; effects can reverse relative to human evidence (ERNIE categorisation relational score 5.30 Chinese vs 6.78 English; Chinese model made fewer objects, d=1.01).
agent_test: Test a persona/language switch on a categorisation task; expect no human-like shift.

claim: Counting measures of 'holism' (objects listed) are confounded by verbosity and English data density; English descriptions listed more objects (10.90 vs 10.06, d=0.36).
agent_test: Normalize outputs by length before comparing styles.

claim: Default LLM outputs resemble WEIRD populations: correlation of -.70 between human-population WEIRDness distance and similarity to GPT output.
agent_test: Test agent's default answers against a non-WEIRD reference sample, abstract-level only so far.

claim: LLM values align closest to Western, English-speaking countries; cultural prompting reduces distance (GPT-4o 2.42 to 1.57) for 71-81% of countries but leaves 19-29% unchanged or worse and a residual bias.
agent_test: Check agent persona prompts against survey data; do not assume persona-prompting fixes bias.

claim: English-centric defaults appear in concrete knowledge as well: ChatGPT answers tie to English culture more than the queried culture; Chinese-trained ERNIE scores 7.6 vs GPT-4 1.8 on Chinese concrete items.
agent_test: Evaluate on locally grounded items per culture.

claim: Survey-alignment results are unstable across prompts: Spearman correlations flip sign (China -0.77 vs +0.54 on a second prompt) and a correct cultural description lifts alignment 1.5 to 2.5.
agent_test: Report across multiple prompt wordings; never one.

claim: Models show human-like content effects on logic tasks (Western participants), a shared bias between humans and LLMs not tied to culture.
agent_test: Test belief bias with content-neutral versus content-conflict versions.

claim: An LLM test of a Nisbett-style task exists but is thin: Atari 2023 ran the triad task 1,100 times (20 triads) against 31 human populations on the same platform and found GPT closest to Netherlands, Finland, Sweden, Ireland (WEIRD). Exact holism percentages are only in figures; no LLM test of change blindness or contradiction tasks was found.
agent_test: Build the battery with human reference data before drawing conclusions.

claim: Vision-language models shift towards 'holistic' captions with Japanese data and few-shot prompts (25.58% to 53.49% holistic), but the judge is GPT-4o and holism is defined as first mention only.
agent_test: Use independent judges and richer operational definitions.

claim: Prompt format changes benchmark accuracy by a median of 7.5 points and up to 76 points (LLaMA-2-13B) with meaning unchanged; format ranking only weakly correlates between models. Single-wording comparisons of models or 'cultures' are unreliable.
agent_test: Report accuracy as a range over at least 5 paraphrases of each item before comparing two agent settings.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Persona prompts do not reliably raise reasoning accuracy: 162 personas on 2,410 MMLU questions gave no significant gain over control; best-persona selection was near random. A role prompt that triggers step-by-step work can help (AQuA 53.5 to 63.8%), but that is a chain-of-thought effect.
agent_test: Test a persona prompt against a plain 'think step by step' control; add personas only if they beat it.

claim: Question language has a small effect on reasoning accuracy (MGSM, PaLM-540B: 44.9% under-resourced vs 47.9% high-resource languages), while values and style measures shift more. Supports a language-neutral reasoning core.
agent_test: Evaluate the agent on translated paraphrases of the same items; expect accuracy to hold and flag drops.

claim: No ablation separates RLHF from pretraining data as the cause of Chinese-vs-US model differences in cultural style. Hu 2026 and Tao 2024 offer RLHF mode collapse as a hypothesis only; Sabir 2025 suggests data content and model matter more than prompt language.
agent_test: Do not rely on a model's 'origin' as a proxy for its style; measure it.

claim: Content-effect and belief-bias human data in LLM comparisons come from one Western sample (UK, N=625 plus 360); human-model shared bias is not shown across cultures.
agent_test: Treat 'models share human biases' as 'models share UK-sample biases'.

claim: The Norenzayan 2002 Study 2 original sample was 52 European American, 52 Asian American, 53 East Asian (N=157); original preregistered contrast East Asian d=0.67, European American d=0.00. Study 1 N was not read.
agent_test: Weight a cross-cultural claim by original N per cell: about 52 per group is small.

claim: Failed-replication details for Peng and Nisbett (Mercier 2015, Chinese vs French) and visual cognition (Hakim 2017) remain abstract-level; exact N, effect sizes and original-author replies were not obtained (paywalled or blocked).
agent_test: Cite these as 'reported null' without numbers until the full text is read.
